messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — SLO breach detected for /v1/stream in us-west-2. p99 > 5s for last 5m. Paging maya_oncall. https://metrics.redwood.example/r/alerts/823

maya_oncall: acked — looking into it now. grabbing dashboards and logs. arnav if I need escalation.

ops-bot: metrics snapshot: p95=420ms, p99=6.2s, error-rate=0.3% over last 5m. active streams concurrent 4.2k.

lucas: seeing a lot of streaming stalls in the runtime logs, lots of 'kv-cache refill' latencies and intermittent EIOs pointing at /dev/nvme1n1 on nodes in shared-gpu-pool-4.

sara: can we get top IO by tenant (5m)? suspect noisy neighbor.

ops-bot: running query: top io by tenant (last 5m)
```
tenant-alpha: 1.2GiB/s
tenant-gamma: 0.95GiB/s
tenant-beta: 0.03GiB/s
```

maya_oncall: tenant-alpha + tenant-gamma both on shared-gpu-pool-4. tenant-alpha looks like large-batch decoding jobs ramping up. that matches the NVMe pressure.

arnav: can we apply IO throttling at cgroup level for tenant-alpha? prefer soft limits first. Suggest io.max to cap write bps.

maya_oncall: agreed — ops, can you apply io cap to tenant-alpha to reduce write bps to ~150MB/s and monitor effects?

ops-bot: applying io.max to tenant-alpha now...
```
# applied: echo "8:0 157286400" > /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-alpha/io.max
# result: write bps limited to ~150MB/s
```

ops-bot: applied successfully. observed write bps drop from 1.2GiB/s -> 140MB/s in ~12s.

lucas: nice — p99 dropped to ~2.1s within two minutes, streaming stalls reduced. p95 steady around 430ms.

jordi_pm: @maya_oncall fyi ACME Corp (acct acme-corp) reported degraded UX moments ago. do we know whether they were affected?

alyssa_cs: ACME calls: several streaming sessions experienced buffering and timeouts. They are on hosted plan, high qps but not dedicated. CS opened a ticket and informed them we're investigating.

maya_oncall: ok — short-term mitigation: migrate tenant-alpha off shared-gpu-pool-4 to dedicated-pool-2 (live migration) to restore isolation. starting migration now. arnav, please take over if any migration issues.

arnav: on it — monitoring migration job 0xabc123.

ops-bot: migration progress: 0% -> 12% -> 55% -> 100%. job 0xabc123 completed; tenant-alpha running on dedicated-pool-2.

arnav: verified migration succeeded. p99 now ~540ms, p95 ~410ms, error-rate down to 0.05%. streaming stalls gone.

maya_oncall: handing off incident to arnav for the next 30m (post-migration watch). I'll draft incident ticket and follow up with a postmortem. immediate action items: 1) IO isolation guardrails for shared pools; 2) auto-detect noisy tenants via IoA (IO anomaly) alerts; 3) add per-tenant streaming stall metrics (p99 tails) to alerting.

jordi_pm: noted. I'll coordinate customer comms for ACME and a follow-up update.

alyssa_cs: CS will send initial status update to ACME: "root cause suspected noisy tenant; mitigation applied; we will follow up with timeline and remediation plan."

maya_oncall: tagging for postmortem: @lucas (runtime), @sara (metrics/alerts), @arnav (infra) — please add your notes. closing page for now. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident resolved — SLOs back within target. Closing pager.
